findings.title: Sustained traffic outpaces retry-record expiry cleanup
findings.why_it_matters: The collector accepts traffic independently across source and visitor quotas, but the scheduler removes only 500 expired events every five minutes. At 200 accepted page entries per minute (for example 200 independent visitors each opening one page), 1,000 records expire between runs while only 500 are removed. The expired backlog grows by 500 each cycle, retaining event-level visitor/product/release associations far beyond the documented two-hour retry window and eventually consuming database capacity. The deliberate per-query batch bound is reasonable, but there is no continuation or draining mechanism to keep retention bounded.
findings.validation_reason: With sustained accepted traffic above 100 events/minute across independent source/visitor quota keys, newly added service.ts:56-64 and index.ts:31 remove only 500 expired rows per five-minute invocation (wrangler.jsonc:32), so the retry-record backlog grows contrary to KTD6's short-term retention requirement; the inspected 501-row cleanup test establishes the batch cap, and production incidence was not measured.

apps/storefront/app/plugins/traffic.client.ts:11: navigator.locks ? navigator.locks.request("shoppp-traffic-identity", operation) : operation(),
findings.suggested_fix: Give identity acquisition (including JSON body consumption) and each event attempt a finite AbortController deadline, clearing the timer in finally. A 10-second deadline is a defensible default for optional analytics. Let the existing catches release the queue and Web Lock after timeout, preserve the identical event ID/body for the existing bounded retry, and add a focused stalled-request test proving later visits can proceed.
findings.title: Bound traffic requests so one stall cannot stop collection
findings.why_it_matters: Integration point without a timeout: both identity and event requests use native fetch without a deadline, while every subsequent route entry waits on the same pending promise. If an identity response, response body, or event response stalls, the affected tab stops collecting every later route entry until that request eventually settles. An identity stall additionally holds the cross-tab Web Lock supplied by the plugin, preventing other tabs from initializing traffic. Shopping remains usable, so this loss is silent in the dashboard rather than a visible page failure.
findings.validation_reason: A stalled identity fetch/body or event fetch in newly added traffic.ts:15-22,42-48 prevents pending.then at line 64 from dispatching later visits, while traffic.client.ts:10 holds the identity Web Lock until that same operation settles; a read-only Bun 1.3.5 probe of the reviewed working-tree client queued two routes, observed only one request while the first remained pending and two after release, confirming reachability with an injected stall, while production incidence was not measured.

testing_gaps: apps/storefront/app/utils/traffic.ts:28-49 introduces expiry renewal and 401/403 identity invalidation, but apps/storefront/tests/traffic.test.ts exercises only a fresh successful ticket, one network retry, and identity network failure. Add fake-clock cases for a later route visit after ticket expiry and a rejected event followed by a later visit; assert renewal, no retry of the rejected event, and a fresh event ID. This proves that ordinary long-lived shopper sessions resume collection without repeatedly submitting a rejected ticket.

apps/admin/src/pages/dashboard/dashboard-page.tsx:254-268 has a separate traffic response generation guard, while dashboard.test.tsx:201-231 defers only revenue for its stale-response test. Revenue's shared financial guard coverage does not exercise this independent success/error guard.

apps/storefront/tests/traffic.test.ts awaits every visit sequentially. Add overlapping A -> B -> A visits while identity initialization or the first delivery is deferred, then release it and assert three distinct entry events in order with one identity initialization. This directly exercises the newly introduced pending queue and lastPath dedup interaction used by app:mounted/page:finish. Existing browser tests cover mount duplication and simultaneous tabs, but not rapid same-tab transitions.
